subject: Marketplace listing: storage routing, deletion timelines, and regional controls

Subject: Marketplace listing — residency/retention questions

Hi Ben,

Thanks for taking this on — we're finalizing our listing for CloudMarket and a few compliance questions came up from our security & legal teams. Can you confirm the following for Redwood Marketplace partner listings (AWS/GCP/Azure):

- Can a partner offer specify a per-customer preferred region (e.g., customer picks AWS us-east-1 vs GCP us-central1) at purchase time?
- Is there any cross-cloud replication for customer data by default?
- How and when is customer data deleted after a termination/termination-for-cause? We need a clear timeline for object store data, model artifacts, KV caches, and logs.
- Who controls backups/snapshots in the marketplace packaging model (partner vs Redwood vs cloud provider)?
- What evidence can you provide (SOC2 summary, dataflow diagram, deletion playbook) to satisfy our auditors?

If you could send a short Q&A or point us at docs, that would be great — ideally before next Tuesday. Happy to set a 30m call if it's easier.

Best,
Lydia

Hi Lydia — thanks, and great questions. High level answers below; Kim (cc'd) will add a few implementation caveats. I can also put together a short mutual action plan and a diagram.

- Per-customer region selection: Yes. Marketplace offers can be configured to honor a customer-selected region at provisioning time. We support routing to AWS/GCP/Azure regions independently and we surface region choices in the purchase flow.

- Cross-cloud replication: Not by default for residency-sensitive paths. We do offer optional multi-region replication for availability, but that is an explicit configuration on the offer and must be disclosed on the listing. For residency-locked offers we disable cross-cloud replication and enforce single-cloud storage.

- Deletion timeline and scope: Our standard deletion chain is: 
  * KV cache entries: invalidated within seconds; eviction fully realized within 7 days depending on TTLs and active sessions.
  * Model artifacts & object storage blobs: deletion job triggers on termination; purge completes within 30 days (cloud provider APIs + lifecycle jobs).
  * Backups/snapshots: separate lifecycle; partners may request expedited snapshot deletion but standard window is 30–90 days depending on snapshot policies.
  * Logs/audit trails: retained according to offer policy; default is 90 days but configurable.

- Backups/snapshots ownership: For Redwood-hosted Marketplace offers, Redwood manages the primary backups (we use cloud provider snapshot APIs). For Redwood Private/Dedicated offers customers can manage snapshots themselves or provide KMS. This will be clearly called out in the offer metadata.

- Evidence for auditors: we can provide a SOC2 summary, a redacted dataflow diagram that shows storage and control plane boundaries, and our deletion playbook.

Next steps: Kim, could you add any constraints around marketplace packaging, particularly how we implement single-cloud enforcement (e.g., replication flags, storage class selection, and service account scopes)? Lydia — will schedule a 30m sync if that helps.

Thanks,
Ben

Hi all — quick technical notes to add to Ben's summary. Putting these here so the marketplace listing is precise about what we enforce vs what is optional.

- Offer-level residency policy: When an offer is set to 'residency locked' we:
  1) Set storage buckets to the selected cloud region (S3/GCS/Azure Blob) and restrict lifecycle/replication flags.
  2) Configure the runtime routing policy so vignettes (inference) only schedule on nodes within that cloud region.
  3) Disable cross-cloud object replication and multi-cloud KV replication.

- Deletion implementation details:
  * Deletion is a two-phase orchestration: 1) Mark resources for deletion and notify the customer; 2) run provider delete APIs and verify success. We track delete jobs in our control plane; artifacts are re-checked 24/72 hours after a delete job to confirm.
  * Object storage purge uses provider DeleteObjects/DeleteMarkers and lifecycle rules; final physical deletion depends on the provider's eventual consistency windows, but we schedule a re-check and report status back to the partner.
  * KV caches and ephemeral session state are invalidated immediately; full clearance is tied to TTL eviction (rarely more than 7 days).

- Backups and snapshots: For Marketplace-hosted offers Redwood typically owns snapshots for manageability. If the partner requires exclusive control we can change packaging to a 'partner-managed snapshot' mode for specific listings.

- Logs & audit trails: Application logs forwarded to Redwood logging pipeline are retained per offer-level settings. We support forwarding logs to customer-managed destinations (e.g., partner S3/GCS) for compliance.

Caveat: If an offer uses cross-cloud object caches for performance (edge caching) we must declare that in the listing; that pattern is not allowed for residency-locked offers.

I'll attach a redacted dataflow diagram and a short deletion checklist for the listing page.

-Kim

- Snapshots/backups: default retention window 30–90 days depending on the snapshot policy for the offer; can be shortened on request for residency-locked offers.
- Logs: default 90 days; can be forwarded to customer-managed sinks or extended/shortened per contract.
